'''Bruno Zumino''' (28 April 1923 − 21 June 2014)<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |date=2014-07-05 |title=Bruno Zumino Dies at 91; Sought to Tie Together Laws of Universe |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/07/05/science/bruno-zumino-sought-to-tie-together-laws-of-universe-dies-at-91.html |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622190725/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/07/05/science/bruno-zumino-sought-to-tie-together-laws-of-universe-dies-at-91.html |archive-date=22 June 2023 }}</ref> was an Italian [[theoretical physicist]] and faculty member at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He obtained his DSc degree from the [[University of Rome La Sapienza|University of Rome]] in 1945.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sanders |first=Robert |url=http://newscenter.berkeley.edu/2014/06/24/bruno-zumino-an-architect-of-supersymmetry-dies-at-91/ |date=June 24, 2014 |title=Bruno Zumino, an architect of supersymmetry, dies at 91 |publisher=Berkeley News |access-date=2014-06-25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140625011026/http://newscenter.berkeley.edu/2014/06/24/bruno-zumino-an-architect-of-supersymmetry-dies-at-91/ |archive-date= 2014-06-25 }}</ref>

He was renowned for his rigorous proof of the [[CPT theorem]] with [[Gerhart Lüders]];<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Lüders | first1 = G. | last2 = Zumino | first2 = B. | doi = 10.1103/PhysRev.110.1450 | title = Connection between Spin and Statistics | journal = Physical Review | volume = 110 | issue = 6 | pages = 1450 | year = 1958 |bibcode = 1958PhRv..110.1450L }}</ref>  his pioneering systematization of effective chiral Lagrangians;<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Coleman | first1 = S. | last2 = Wess | first2 = J. | last3 = Zumino | first3 = B. | doi = 10.1103/PhysRev.177.2239 | title = Structure of Phenomenological Lagrangians. I | journal = Physical Review | volume = 177 | issue = 5 | pages = 2239 | year = 1969 |bibcode = 1969PhRv..177.2239C }}; {{Cite journal | last1 = Callan | first1 = C. | last2 = Coleman | first2 = S. | last3 = Wess | first3 = J. | last4 = Zumino | first4 = B. | title = Structure of Phenomenological Lagrangians. II | doi = 10.1103/PhysRev.177.2247 | journal = Physical Review | volume = 177 | issue = 5 | pages = 2247 | year = 1969 |bibcode = 1969PhRv..177.2247C }}</ref>  the discoveries, with [[Julius Wess]], of the [[Wess–Zumino model]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Wess | first1 = J. | last2 = Zumino | first2 = B. | doi = 10.1016/0550-3213(74)90355-1 | title = Supergauge transformations in four dimensions | journal = Nuclear Physics B | volume = 70 | issue = 1 | pages = 39–50 | year = 1974 |bibcode = 1974NuPhB..70...39W | url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/201649/files/CM-P00060236.pdf }}</ref>  the first four-dimensional [[supersymmetric]] [[quantum field theory]] with Bose–Fermi degeneracy, and initiator of the field of supersymmetric radiative restrictions;  a concise formulation of [[supergravity]];<ref>Deser, S., & Zumino, B. (1976). "Consistent supergravity", ''Physics Letters''  ''' B62''' 335-337. {{doi|10.1016/0370-2693(76)90089-7}}</ref>
and for his deciphering of structured flavour-chiral anomalies, codified in the  [[Wess–Zumino–Witten model]] of [[conformal field theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Wess | first1 = J. | last2 = Zumino | first2 = B. | doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(71)90582-X | title = Consequences of anomalous ward identities | journal = Physics Letters B | volume = 37 | issue = 1 | pages = 95–97 | year = 1971 |bibcode = 1971PhLB...37...95W | url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/486885/files/CM-P00058941.pdf }}</ref>

==Awards==
* 1985 [[List of members of the National Academy of Sciences (Physics)|Membership]] in the [[National Academy of Sciences]]

* 1988 [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]]
* 1989 [[Max Planck Medal]]
* 1992 [[Wigner Medal]]
* 1992 [[Humboldt Research Award]]
* 1999 Gian Carlo Wick Commemorative Gold Medal
